transcript: You know you're a hardcore theater person when you attend an eight hour show like Gatz at The Public. This epic adaptation of The Great Gatsby features the entire novel word for word as its text. This work was developed by Elevator Repair Service and first premiered in New York 20 years ago, and despite its length, it has stood the test of time and this encore production still features much of the original cast which is pretty cool. I actually had not read the novel but I knew the story, which I'm honestly not really a fan of, but this was an undeniably impressive production. So basically, it starts with this guy in an office who picks up a copy of the book and starts reading it, and then the entire story happens all around him with coworkers transforming into the characters and the office assuming various settings in the book. From an artistic point of view and as an adaptation this is brilliant in many ways. Oftentimes classics are hard to adapt because you have to handle the fact that some people are gonna come in with really strong feelings and preconceived notions about the characterizations or visualizations of certain scenes and characters. Gatz completely avoids this issue altogether by subverting expectations in really fresh and inventive ways. By dropping us into an office with everyday people, it's so far from the way you would expect the story to look if you're just reading the novel. And the way it playfully juxtaposes the poetic language and cinematic descriptions in the novel with casual and understated enactments using office supplies creates a lot of humorous and unexpected moments that you just cannot capture with any other art form but theatre. As far as my experience, I enjoyed it. I can't say it made me suddenly love The Great Gatsby but it was a really cool, truly one of a kind piece of theater. And yes, it was long. Because of that, I can't in good faith say that this will be for everyone. Although I didn't feel like it ever dragged, there were points which were somewhat slow and meditative — not unlike the experience of actually reading a novel. And with roughly six hours of total stage time, this will be an intimidating piece if you're not a theater person or at least a big Gatsby fan. But if you're up for it, it is definitely worth your while, especially since it's likely gonna be the last time this production is staged in New York.
